messages.subject: Problems with a very simple path model
parts:
Hi all

I have just started using lavaan today ! I am an instructor on an introductory SEM module. Stata is used throughout the module but we also give R code, and having done some basic research I have decided to use lavaan ! However I am having trouble with one particular simple path model. In Stata, the model looks like:


clear all
ssd init EE DR RO SE 
ssd set observations 321

ssd set sd 15.23 10.15 16.27 1.01 

ssd set correlations ///
 1 \ ///
 0.25 1 \ ///
 0.78 0.21 1 \ ///
 -0.47 -0.27 -0.35 1

 sem (SE -> EE) (EE -> DR) (EE -> RO) (DR -> RO), nocapslatent

This produces the following output (which also agrees with MPlus)

Iteration 0:   log likelihood = -4135.5673  
Iteration 1:   log likelihood = -4135.5673  

Structural equation model                       Number of obs      =       321
Estimation method  = ml
Log likelihood     = -4135.5673
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
             |                 OIM
             |      Coef.   Std. Err.      z    P>|z|     [95% Conf. Interval]
-------------+----------------------------------------------------------------
Structural   |
  EE <-      |
          SE |  -7.087228   .7428868    -9.54   0.000    -8.543259   -5.631196
  -----------+----------------------------------------------------------------
  DR <-      |
          EE |    .166612   .0360163     4.63   0.000     .0960213    .2372026
  -----------+----------------------------------------------------------------
  RO <-      |
          EE |   .8289902   .0385246    21.52   0.000     .7534834    .9044969
          DR |   .0256473   .0578058     0.44   0.657      -.08765    .1389446
-------------+----------------------------------------------------------------
Variance     |
        e.EE |   180.1515   14.22003                      154.3297    210.2938
        e.DR |   96.28271   7.599951                      82.48212    112.3924
        e.RO |   103.2753   8.151902                      88.47244    120.5549
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LR test of model vs. saturated: chi2(2)   =     10.78, Prob > chi2 = 0.0046


Using lavaan, I have tried to fit this model as follows:

vars <- c("SE","EE","DR","RO")
sds <- c(1.01, 15.23, 10.15, 16.27)


lower.cormat <- '
1,
0.25, 1,
0.78, 0.21, 1 ,
-0.47, -0.27, -0.35, 1
'

cormat <- getCov(lower.cormat,names=vars)

covmat <- cor2cov(cormat,sds)

cleary.model <- '
EE ~ SE
DR ~ EE
RO ~ EE
RO ~ DR
'
fit <- sem(cleary.model, sample.cov=covmat, sample.nobs=321)
summary(fit, standardized=TRUE)

However the output I get is:


  Number of observations                           321

  Estimator                                         ML
  Minimum Function Test Statistic              320.494
  Degrees of freedom                                 2
  P-value (Chi-square)                           0.000

Parameter estimates:

  Information                                 Expected
  Standard Errors                             Standard

                   Estimate  Std.err  Z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv  Std.all
Regressions:
  EE ~
    SE                3.770    0.815    4.626    0.000    3.770    0.250
  DR ~
    EE                0.140    0.036    3.848    0.000    0.140    0.210
  RO ~
    EE               -0.220    0.056   -3.936    0.000   -0.220   -0.206
    DR               -0.492    0.084   -5.874    0.000   -0.492   -0.307

Variances:
    EE              216.778   17.111                    216.778    0.938
    DR               98.172    7.749                     98.172    0.956

Could anyone tell me where I am going wrong ?

Thanks
RL

messages.subject: Re: Problems with a very simple path model
parts: It seems to me that the order of standard deviations are different between two models. In the Stata, you used

but in R you used

c(1.01, 15.23, 10.15, 16.27)

The variable names corresponding to rows and columns in the correlation matrix in both analyses are different too. The following script should match Stata and Mplus

vars <- c("EE","DR","RO","SE")
sds <- c(15.23, 10.15, 16.27, 1.01)

lower.cormat <- '
1,
0.25, 1,
0.78, 0.21, 1 ,
-0.47, -0.27, -0.35, 1
'
cormat <- getCov(lower.cormat,names=vars)
covmat <- cor2cov(cormat,sds)
cleary.model <- '
EE ~ SE
DR ~ EE
RO ~ EE
RO ~ DR
'
fit <- sem(cleary.model, sample.cov=covmat, sample.nobs=321)
summary(fit, standardized=TRUE)

Minimum Function Test Statistic               10.781
  Degrees of freedom                                 2
  P-value (Chi-square)                           0.005

Sunthud
